UpdateYPosNoGrvty.name: Update sprite Y position, no gravity
summary: Adds the sprite's Y speed to its Y position: speed/16 whole pixels plus a 4-bit fraction kept in [$14EC+X] (the speed is 1/16 px per frame).
Parameters: X: sprite index.
Returns: [$1491] = amount the sprite moved (whole pixels).
Also contains an unused routine at $02D2C7 and the 'aim at Mario' routine at $02D2FB (sets [$00] = Y speed, [$01] = X speed pointing at Mario,
for a given speed in A, with the longer distance getting the full speed). Nothing calls $02D2FB except the unused code.

s02D374.name: Data: sprite height offsets for GetDrawInfo2
summary: $02D374: $0C, $1C - Y offsets tested against the screen. $02D376: $01, $02 - the offscreen-vertical bit set for each.

GetDrawInfo2.name: Get sprite draw info (bank 2)
summary: Bank 2 copy of GetDrawInfo. Sets the horizontal/vertical offscreen flags and [$15C4,X] (1 = more than $40 px offscreen horizontally),
then returns the sprite's position on screen.
Parameters: X: sprite index.
Returns: Y = OAM index of the sprite, [$00] = X on screen, [$01] = Y on screen.
Quirk: if the sprite is far offscreen horizontally it pops its own return address and returns to the caller's caller (skips drawing).

Layer3SmashMain.name: Layer 3 smash: main
summary: Sprite $89. Puts the layer 3 scroll at the sprite's position (CODE_00FF61), checks Mario against it, follows the screen scroll in X
and runs the state routine.

Layer3SmashPtrs.name: Layer 3 smash: states and Mario collision
summary: State pointers: 0 wait ([$1540]) then pick a random X in $FF80-$FFBF and Y = 0; 1 slide down at speed 4 until the timer ends;
2 fall with gravity (+7, max $40) until Y >= $A0, then snap to the floor, shake the ground ([$1887] = $50), sound $09, timer $30;
3 rest; 4 rise at speed $E0 until Y = 0, then back to state 0 with a $A0 frame timer.
$02D49C: collision with Mario. Mario below the smasher's bottom and within the central $80 px: hurt if on the ground, otherwise
his Y speed is set to the smasher's. In the $08 px margins at either side Mario is pushed sideways (X speed +8 or $F8).

s02D4F2.name: Unused data: bit masks
summary: $80, $40, ... $01. Unreferenced.

s02D4FA.name: Mario/sprite horizontal and vertical distance
summary: $02D4FA: Y = 0 if Mario is to the right of (or level with) the sprite, 1 if to the left; [$0F] = low byte of Mario X - sprite X.
$02D50C: Y = 0 if Mario is below (or level with) the sprite, 1 if above; [$0E] = low byte of Mario Y - sprite Y.
Parameters: X: sprite index.

s02D57F.name: Data: sound effect numbers
summary: $FF, $13-$19. Indexed by Y in code at $02F2C0 (which looks unreachable).

s02D587.name: Banzai Bill main
summary: Draws the Banzai Bill, then (unless killed or sprites are locked) erases it when offscreen, moves it left at speed $E8 (-24)
and handles contact with Mario.

s02D5A4.name: Data: Banzai Bill tile X offsets

s02D5B4.name: Data: Banzai Bill tile Y offsets

BanzaiBillTiles.name: Draw Banzai Bill (4x4 tiles)
summary: Tile numbers and properties, then the draw routine at $02D5E4: 16 tiles of 16x16 in a 4x4 block ($40 px square), last row Y-flipped.
Parameters: X: sprite index.

Banzai+Rotating.name: Banzai Bill, ball and chain, chained platform
summary: Entry for sprites $9E (ball and chain), $9F (Banzai Bill) and $A3 (grey platform on chain); sets the data bank first.
Rotating sprites ($02D62A): angle [$151C+X]:[$1602+X] (9-bit) changes by +/-2 per frame; direction = bit 4 of the sprite's X position.
Offset from the pivot = radius [$187B+X] * sin/cos (table CircleCoords, rounded using the hardware multiplier). The sprite is moved there,
[$1528+X] gets the X distance moved this frame (for carrying Mario), then interaction and drawing run and the sprite goes back to the pivot.
Ball and chain: MarioSprInteract and a 4-tile ball. Platform: solid block via InvisBlkMainRt and a wooden platform. Both draw 2 chain links
at 32 px and 16 px from the pivot along the line to the ball. $02D870: A = A * 32 / radius (signed), using the hardware divider.
Notes: NOPs at $02D800 are timing delays after hardware multiply/divide; they also serve as the ball tile number ($EA).

s02D807.name: Data: ball and chain tile layout
summary: X offsets, Y offsets and properties for the four 16x16 ball tiles.

s02D813.name: Draw ball of ball and chain
summary: Draws a 32x32 ball from four copies of tile $EA with different flips (tile read from the NOPs at $02D800).
Parameters: X: sprite index.
